tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

schema.name: Write

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

157	type slowStartController struct {
158		mu             sync.Mutex
159		maxConnections int
160		totalLaunched  int
161		batchPending   int           // Connections in current batch waiting for HTTP response
162		batchReady     int           // Connections in current batch that succeeded
163		nextBatchSize  int           // Next batch size: 1, 2, 4, 16, 256... (capped)

168	func newSlowStartController(maxConnections int) *slowStartController {
169		return &slowStartController{
170			maxConnections: maxConnections,
171			nextBatchSize:  1,
172			expansionCh:    make(chan struct{}, 1),
173		}
174	}
175	
176	// onConnectSuccess is called when a connection successfully gets HTTP response
177	// Returns true if this completes the current batch
178	func (s *slowStartController) onConnectSuccess() bool {
179		s.mu.Lock()
180		defer s.mu.Unlock()
181	
182		s.batchReady++
183		if s.batchReady >= s.batchPending {
184			// Batch complete, signal expansion
185			select {
186			case s.expansionCh <- struct{}{}:
187			default:
188			}
189			return true
190		}
191		return false
192	}
193	
194	// onConnectFailed is called when a connection fails
195	func (s *slowStartController) onConnectFailed() {
196		s.mu.Lock()
197		defer s.mu.Unlock()
198	
199		// Reduce pending count
200		if s.batchPending > 0 {
201			s.batchPending--
202		}
203		// If all pending resolved (success or fail), trigger expansion
204		// This handles both successful completion and all-failures case
205		if s.batchPending == 0 {
206			select {
207			case s.expansionCh <- struct{}{}:
208			default:
209			}
210		}
211	}
212	
213	// getNextBatchSize returns how many connections to start in next batch
214	// Returns 0 if max reached
215	func (s *slowStartController) getNextBatchSize() int {
216		s.mu.Lock()
217		defer s.mu.Unlock()
218	
219		if s.paused {
220			return 0
221		}
222	
223		remaining := s.maxConnections - s.totalLaunched
224		if remaining <= 0 {
225			return 0
226		}
227	
228		batchSize := s.nextBatchSize
229		if batchSize > remaining {
230			batchSize = remaining
231		}
232	
233		return batchSize
234	}

236	// commitBatch confirms that a batch of connections is being launched
237	func (s *slowStartController) commitBatch(count int) {
238		s.mu.Lock()
239		defer s.mu.Unlock()
240	
241		s.totalLaunched += count
242		if s.nextBatchSize == 1 {
243			// Bootstrap growth: squaring one would never increase the batch size.
244			s.nextBatchSize = min(2, s.maxConnections)
245		} else if s.nextBatchSize > s.maxConnections/s.nextBatchSize {
246			// Cap before multiplying to avoid integer overflow.
247			s.nextBatchSize = s.maxConnections
248		} else {
249			s.nextBatchSize *= s.nextBatchSize
250		}
251		s.batchPending = count
252		s.batchReady = 0
253	}

346	func (f *Fetcher) Setup(ctl *controller.Controller) {
347		f.ctl = ctl
348		f.doneCh = make(chan error, 1)
349		if f.meta == nil {
350			f.meta = &fetcher.FetcherMeta{}
351		}
352		f.ctl.GetConfig(&f.config)
353		if f.impersonationSession == nil {
354			f.impersonationSession = httpclient.NewImpersonationSession()
355		}
356		f.resolvedCh = make(chan struct{})
357		f.primaryReadyCh = make(chan struct{})
358	
359		// Check if this is a restore scenario (has existing connections or meta)
360		if f.meta.Res != nil {
361			// Already resolved, close the channel immediately
362			close(f.resolvedCh)
363			f.state.Store(int32(stateResolved))
364		} else {
365			f.state.Store(int32(stateIdle))
366		}
367	}

419	func (f *Fetcher) Resolve(req *base.Request) error {
420		if err := base.ParseReqExtra[fhttp.ReqExtra](req); err != nil {
421			return err
422		}
423		f.meta.Req = req
424	
425		f.setState(stateResolving)
426	
427		// Build HTTP request WITHOUT Range header (normal request)
428		// This allows the response to be reused for downloading (important for one-time URLs)
429		// The body outlives Resolve, so the read timeout gets its own cancel func.
430		reqCtx, reqCancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
431		httpReq, err := f.buildRequest(reqCtx, req)
432		if err != nil {
433			reqCancel()
434			f.setState(stateError)
435			return err
436		}
437	
438		client := f.buildClient()
439	
440		// Send normal HTTP request (no Range header)
441		// Track connection time for adaptive timeout in download phase
442		connStartTime := time.Now()
443		resp, err := client.Do(httpReq)
444		if err != nil {
445			reqCancel()
446			f.setState(stateError)
447			return err
448		}
449		// Record connection time as baseline for fast-fail timeout
450		f.updateMaxConnTime(time.Since(connStartTime))
451	
452		// Parse response to get resource info
453		res := &base.Resource{
454			Range: false,
455			Files: []*base.FileInfo{},
456		}
457	
458		if resp.StatusCode != base.HttpCodeOK && resp.StatusCode != base.HttpCodePartialContent {
459			resp.Body.Close()
460			reqCancel()
461			f.setState(stateError)
462			return NewRequestError(resp.StatusCode)
463		}
464	
465		// Check if server supports range requests
466		acceptRanges := resp.Header.Get(base.HttpHeaderAcceptRanges)
467		contentRange := resp.Header.Get(base.HttpHeaderContentRange)
468		if acceptRanges == base.HttpHeaderBytes || strings.HasPrefix(contentRange, base.HttpHeaderBytes) {
469			res.Range = true
470		}
471	
472		// A partial response describes one segment, not the whole resource.
473		reuseResolveBody := true
474		if resp.StatusCode == base.HttpCodePartialContent {
475			start, _, total, err := parseRangeResponse(resp)
476			if err != nil {
477				resp.Body.Close()
478				reqCancel()
479				f.setState(stateError)
480				return err
481			}
482			res.Size = total
483			res.Range = true
484			// Prefetch is a contiguous prefix copied at offset zero. A segment
485			// starting elsewhere must be fetched again through the Range path.
486			reuseResolveBody = start == 0
487		} else {
488			contentLength := resp.Header.Get(base.HttpHeaderContentLength)
489			if contentLength != "" {
490				if size, err := strconv.ParseInt(contentLength, 10, 64); err == nil {
491					res.Size = size
492				}
493			}
494		}
495		// A hint is only a display value, even when the origin advertises Range.
496		known := resp.StatusCode == base.HttpCodePartialContent || resp.ContentLength >= 0
497		f.sizeKnown = &known
498		f.sequentialSizeUnknown = !res.Range && !known
499		if !known {
500			res.Size = f.sizeHint()
501		}
502	
503		// Parse last modified time
504		var lastModifiedTime *time.Time
505		lastModified := resp.Header.Get(base.HttpHeaderLastModified)
506		if lastModified != "" {
507			if t, err := http.ParseTime(lastModified); err == nil {
508				lastModifiedTime = &t
509			}
510		}
511		f.ifRange = extractIfRangeValidator(resp.Header)
512	
513		file := &base.FileInfo{
514			Size:  res.Size,
515			Ctime: lastModifiedTime,
516		}
517	
518		// Parse filename
519		contentDisposition := resp.Header.Get(base.HttpHeaderContentDisposition)
520		if contentDisposition != "" {
521			file.Name = parseFilename(contentDisposition)
522		}
523		if file.Name == "" {
524			file.Name = path.Base(httpReq.URL.Path)
525			if file.Name != "" {
526				// Use PathUnescape instead of QueryUnescape to correctly handle %2B (should decode to +, not space)
527				file.Name, _ = url.PathUnescape(file.Name)
528			}
529		}
530		if file.Name == "" || file.Name == "/" || file.Name == "." {
531			file.Name = httpReq.URL.Hostname()
532		}
533		file.Name = appendFilenameExtension(file.Name, resp.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
534	
535		res.Files = append(res.Files, file)
536		f.meta.Res = res
537	
538		// Save redirect URL for later connections
539		f.redirectURL = resp.Request.URL.String()
540	
541		// IMPORTANT: Keep the response body open for downloading in Start phase
542		// This is crucial for one-time URLs that can only be accessed once
543		f.resolveRespLock.Lock()
544		if reuseResolveBody {
545			f.resolveResp = resp
546			f.resolveRespCancel = reqCancel
547		} else {
548			resp.Body.Close()
549			reqCancel()
550			f.prefetchDone.Store(true)
551		}
552		f.resolveRespLock.Unlock()
553	
554		f.setState(stateResolved)
555	
556		// Signal that resolve is complete
557		f.resolvedOnce.Do(func() {
558			close(f.resolvedCh)
559		})
560	
561		// Start async prefetch in background (only for range-supported resources)
562		// For non-range resources, the response will be used directly in Start
563		if res.Range && reuseResolveBody {
564			f.prefetchStopCh = make(chan struct{})
565			f.resolveFallback.Store(true)
566			go f.asyncPrefetch()
567		}
568	
569		// If start was called before resolve completed, auto-start
570		if f.startPending.Load() {
571			go f.doStart()
572		}
573	
574		return nil
575	}

577	// asyncPrefetch downloads data in background during resolve phase
578	// This data can be reused when Start is called to save time
579	func (f *Fetcher) asyncPrefetch() {
580		defer func() {
581			f.prefetchDone.Store(true)
582		}()
583	
584		// Get the resolve response
585		f.resolveRespLock.Lock()
586		resp, cancel := f.resolveResp, f.resolveRespCancel
587		f.resolveRespLock.Unlock()
588	
589		if resp == nil {
590			return
591		}
592	
593		defer func() {
594			// Close the response even if temporary-file setup fails or shutdown
595			// rejects a late prefetch. Otherwise the server can remain blocked writing.
596			f.resolveRespLock.Lock()
597			f.closeResolveRespLocked()
598			f.resolveRespLock.Unlock()
599		}()
600	
601		// Create temporary file for prefetch data
602		tempDir := ""
603		if f.ctl != nil && f.ctl.TempDir != "" {
604			tempDir = f.ctl.TempDir
605			if err := os.MkdirAll(tempDir, 0700); err != nil {
606				f.prefetchErr = err
607				return
608			}
609		}
610		tmpFile, err := os.CreateTemp(tempDir, "gopeed-prefetch-*")
611		if err != nil {
612			f.prefetchErr = err
613			return
614		}
615		if f.ctl != nil {
616			if err := f.ctl.TempFiles.Track(tmpFile.Name()); err != nil {
617				tmpFile.Close()
618				os.Remove(tmpFile.Name())
619				f.prefetchErr = err
620				return
621			}
622		}
623		f.prefetchFile = tmpFile
624		f.prefetchFilePath = tmpFile.Name()
625	
626		buf := make([]byte, 32*1024) // 32KB buffer
627		reader := f.responseReader(resp, cancel)
628	
629		for {
630			select {
631			case <-f.prefetchStopCh:
632				// Stop signal received (Start was called)
633				return
634			default:
635			}
636	
637			n, err := reader.Read(buf)
638			if n > 0 {
639				_, writeErr := tmpFile.Write(buf[:n])
640				if writeErr != nil {
641					f.prefetchErr = writeErr
642					return
643				}
644				f.prefetchSize.Add(int64(n))
645			}
646			if err != nil {
647				if err == io.EOF {
648					// Prefetch completed
649					return
650				}
651				f.prefetchErr = err
652				return
653			}
654		}
655	}

657	// stopPrefetchAndGetData stops the async prefetch and returns prefetched bytes
658	// It also copies prefetched data to the target file
659	func (f *Fetcher) stopPrefetchAndCopyData() int64 {
660		// Signal prefetch to stop (safely)
661		if f.prefetchStopCh != nil {
662			select {
663			case <-f.prefetchStopCh:
664				// Already closed
665			default:
666				close(f.prefetchStopCh)
667			}
668		}
669	
670		// Wait for prefetch to finish (with timeout)
671		for i := 0; f.prefetchStopCh != nil && i < 1000 && !f.prefetchDone.Load(); i++ {
672			time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
673		}
674	
675		prefetched := f.prefetchSize.Load()
676		if prefetched == 0 {
677			f.cleanupPrefetchFile()
678			return 0
679		}
680	
681		// Copy prefetch data to target file
682		if f.prefetchFile != nil && f.file != nil {
683			// Seek to beginning of prefetch file
684			f.prefetchFile.Seek(0, io.SeekStart)
685	
686			// Copy to target file at position 0
687			buf := make([]byte, 32*1024)
688			var copied int64
689			for copied < prefetched {
690				n, err := f.prefetchFile.Read(buf)
691				if n > 0 {
692					f.file.WriteAt(buf[:n], copied)
693					copied += int64(n)
694				}
695				if err != nil {
696					break
697				}
698			}
699		}
700	
701		f.cleanupPrefetchFile()
702		return prefetched
703	}

705	// cleanupPrefetchFile closes and removes the prefetch temporary file
706	func (f *Fetcher) cleanupPrefetchFile() {
707		if f.prefetchFile != nil {
708			f.prefetchFile.Close()
709			f.prefetchFile = nil
710		}
711		if f.prefetchFilePath != "" {
712			if f.ctl != nil {
713				f.ctl.TempFiles.Remove(f.prefetchFilePath)
714			} else {
715				os.Remove(f.prefetchFilePath)
716			}
717			f.prefetchFilePath = ""
718		}
719		// The byte count is only reusable while the backing prefetch file exists.
720		// Pause may discard that file before the first Start, so retaining the
721		// count would make the next Start skip bytes that were never copied.
722		f.prefetchSize.Store(0)
723		f.resolveFallback.Store(false)
724	}

726	// prepareFullRedownload resets all fetcher connection and prefetch state
727	// after a checksum mismatch so the subsequent Start takes the fresh-start path.
728	func (f *Fetcher) prepareFullRedownload() {
729		f.connMu.Lock()
730		if f.meta.Res.Range {
731			f.connections = nil
732			f.resolveConn = nil
733			f.rangeReprobeEligible = false
734			f.rangeValidatorPinned = false
735		}
736		f.connMu.Unlock()
737	
738		f.cleanupPrefetchFile()
739		f.resolveDataPos.Store(0)
740	}

742	// Options may be replaced between Resolve and Start when creating a resolved task.
743	func (f *Fetcher) initOptions() error {
744		if f.meta.Opts == nil {
745			f.meta.Opts = &base.Options{}
746		}
747		opts := f.meta.Opts
748		// Parse options
749		if err := base.ParseOptExtra[fhttp.OptsExtra](opts); err != nil {
750			return err
751		}
752		if opts.Extra == nil {
753			opts.Extra = &fhttp.OptsExtra{}
754		}
755		extra := opts.Extra.(*fhttp.OptsExtra)
756		if extra.Connections <= 0 {
757			extra.Connections = f.config.Connections
758			if extra.Connections <= 0 {
759				extra.Connections = 1
760			}
761		}
762		if err := extra.Checksum.Validate(); err != nil {
763			return err
764		}
765	
766		return nil
767	}

769	func (f *Fetcher) Start() error {
770		if err := f.initOptions(); err != nil {
771			return err
772		}
773		state := f.getState()
774	
775		switch state {
776		case stateResolved, statePaused:
777			// Normal case: resolved or resuming from pause
778			return f.doStart()
779	
780		case stateResolving:
781			// Early start: mark pending and return immediately
782			f.startPending.Store(true)
783			return nil
784	
785		case stateSlowStart, stateSteady:
786			// Already downloading, this is a resume from pause
787			return f.doStart()
788	
789		case stateError:
790			// Retry after error: reset and restart
791			return f.doStart()
792	
793		default:
794			return fmt.Errorf("cannot start in current state: %v", state)
795		}
796	}

798	func (f *Fetcher) doStart() error {
799		// Wait for resolve to complete
800		<-f.resolvedCh
801	
802		state := f.getState()
803		if state == stateDone {
804			return nil
805		}
806	
807		// Each Start/Wait cycle must observe only its own completion result.
808		// A paused or failed cycle may have completed concurrently with Pause and
809		// left a result buffered before its download loop fully stopped.
810		if state == statePaused || state == stateError {
811			select {
812			case <-f.doneCh:
813			default:
814			}
815		}
816	
817		// If retrying after error, reset connection states for retry
818		if state == stateError {
819			fullRedownload := f.checksumFailed.Swap(false)
820			if fullRedownload {
821				// Checksum mismatch: the file content itself is wrong even
822				// though every connection reported Completed. Truncate the
823				// corrupt file so stale bytes cannot linger if the retry is
824				// interrupted before every connection re-writes its chunk.
825				if err := os.Truncate(f.meta.SingleFilepath(), 0); err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
826					return fmt.Errorf("failed to reset file after checksum mismatch: %w", err)
827				}
828				f.prepareFullRedownload()
829			}
830			f.connMu.Lock()
831			for _, conn := range f.connections {
832				// On a normal error, only reset connections that didn't
833				// finish. On a checksum mismatch, reset EVERY connection —
834				// "Completed" only means the download loop finished, not
835				// that the bytes were verified correct.
836				shouldReset := fullRedownload || (!conn.Completed && conn.State != connCompleted)
837				if shouldReset {
838					if fullRedownload || !f.hasSequentialPrefixLocked(conn) {
839						f.resetConnectionForRestart(conn)
840					}
841					conn.State = connNotStarted
842					conn.failed = false
843					conn.retryTimes = 0
844					conn.lastErr = nil
845				}
846			}
847			f.connMu.Unlock()
848		}
849	
850		// Open or create target file first (needed for prefetch copy)
851		name := f.meta.SingleFilepath()
852		var err error
853		var file *os.File
854		_, err = os.Stat(name)
855		if err != nil {
856			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
857				file, err = f.ctl.Touch(name, f.knownSize())
858			} else {
859				return err
860			}
861		} else {
862			file, err = os.OpenFile(name, os.O_RDWR, os.ModeAppend)
863		}
864		if err != nil {
865			return err
866		}
867		f.fileMu.Lock()
868		f.file = file
869		f.fileMu.Unlock()
870	
871		// For range-supported resources, stop prefetch and copy data
872		// For non-range resources, the response will be used directly
873		var prefetchedBytes int64
874		if f.meta.Res.Range {
875			resolveComplete := f.knownSize() > 0 && f.prefetchDone.Load() && f.prefetchErr == nil && f.prefetchSize.Load() >= f.knownSize()
876			if f.resolveFallback.Load() && !resolveComplete {
877				// Keep Resolve downloading until the first Range response has been
878				// validated. The Range request starts at a stable snapshot; a valid
879				// takeover discards any overlap downloaded by Resolve in the meantime.
880				prefetchedBytes = f.prefetchSize.Load()
881			} else {
882				// Resolve already completed, or no live Resolve fallback remains.
883				prefetchedBytes = f.stopPrefetchAndCopyData()
884			}
885			f.resolveDataPos.Store(prefetchedBytes)
886	
887			if !f.resolveFallback.Load() {
888				// Also close resolve response if still open.
889				f.resolveRespLock.Lock()
890				f.closeResolveRespLocked()
891				f.resolveRespLock.Unlock()
892			}
893		}
894	
895		// Avoid request extra modified by extension
896		if err = base.ParseReqExtra[fhttp.ReqExtra](f.meta.Req); err != nil {
897			return err
898		}
899	
900		// Initialize slow start controller
901		maxConns := f.meta.Opts.Extra.(*fhttp.OptsExtra).Connections
902		f.slowStart = newSlowStartController(maxConns)
903	
904		// Create main context
905		f.ctx, f.cancel = context.WithCancel(context.Background())
906	
907		// Create downloadLoop lifecycle channel
908		downloadLoopDone := make(chan struct{})
909		f.downloadLoopDone = downloadLoopDone
910	
911		// Start download
912		f.setState(stateSlowStart)
913		go f.downloadLoop(downloadLoopDone)
914	
915		return nil
916	}
917	
918	func (f *Fetcher) downloadLoop(done chan struct{}) {
919		ctx := f.ctx
920	
921		defer func() {
922			// Update file last modified time before closing
923			if f.config.UseServerCtime && f.meta.Res.Files[0].Ctime != nil {
924				setft.SetFileTime(f.meta.SingleFilepath(), time.Now(), *f.meta.Res.Files[0].Ctime, *f.meta.Res.Files[0].Ctime)
925			}
926	
927			// Signal that downloadLoop has exited
928			if done != nil {
929				close(done)
930			}
931		}()
932	
933		// Check if this is a resume or fresh start
934		isResume := len(f.connections) > 0
935	
936		if !isResume {
937			// Capture the mode before launching the first connection. The server may
938			// ignore that connection's Range request and switch the fetcher to a
939			// sequential download while the request is in flight.
940			startedWithRanges := f.meta.Res.Range
941			// Fresh start: begin with resolve connection
942			f.startResolveDownload()
943			// Non-range downloads wait for their only connection in
944			// startResolveDownload. Falling through would consume the connection's
945			// expansion signal and publish the same completion a second time.
946			if !startedWithRanges || f.getState() == stateDone {
947				return
948			}
949		} else {
950			// A retained sequential prefix starts as the first slow-start batch. If
951			// its guarded request restores Range support, the normal expansion loop
952			// can split the remaining suffix across the configured connections.
953			canRecoverRange := f.hasSequentialRecoveryCandidate()
954			if canRecoverRange {
955				f.slowStart.commitBatch(1)
956			}
957			f.resumeConnections()
958			if !canRecoverRange {
959				f.waitForCompletion(ctx)
960				return
961			}
962		}
963	
964		// Slow start loop
965		for {
966			select {
967			case <-ctx.Done():
968				// Paused or cancelled
969				return
970			case <-f.slowStart.expansionCh:
971				f.connMu.Lock()
972				rangeMode := f.meta.Res.Range
973				sequentialExited := len(f.connections) == 1 && f.connections[0].exited
974				f.connMu.Unlock()
975				if !rangeMode {
976					// The primary response is still being consumed sequentially. A
977					// successful re-probe or final connection exit will signal again.
978					if sequentialExited {
979						f.waitForCompletion(ctx)
980						return
981					}
982					continue
983				}
984				// Batch completed, try to expand
985				if f.checkCompletion() {
986					// All work is done, wait for connections to finish
987					f.waitForCompletion(ctx)
988					return
989				}
990				f.expandConnections()
991	
992				// Check if we've reached steady state (max connections)
993				if f.getState() == stateSteady {
994					// Wait for all connections to complete
995					f.waitForCompletion(ctx)
996					return
997				}
998			}
999		}
1000	}
1001	
1002	func (f *Fetcher) startResolveDownload() {
1003		// Without Range support, consume the reusable Resolve response sequentially.
1004		// A Range-capable resource with an unknown size instead starts one open-ended
1005		// worker, which discovers the total from Content-Range before slow-start expands.
1006		if !f.meta.Res.Range {
1007			// Create a single connection for the entire file
1008			conn := &connection{
1009				ID:    0,
1010				Role:  rolePrimary,
1011				State: connNotStarted,
1012				Chunk: newChunk(0, 0), // For non-range, end doesn't matter
1013			}
1014			conn.ctx, conn.cancel = context.WithCancel(f.ctx)
1015			f.connMu.Lock()
1016			f.connections = append(f.connections, conn)
1017			f.connMu.Unlock()
1018	
1019			f.wg.Add(1)
1020			// Use the resolve response directly
1021			go f.runConnectionWithResolveResp(conn)
1022	
1023			// For non-range downloads, wait for completion directly in this goroutine
1024			// Don't create another goroutine to avoid WaitGroup reuse issues
1025			f.waitForCompletion(f.ctx)
1026			return
1027		}
1028	
1029		// Range supported: use slow start to launch connections
1030		// Start first batch of connections
1031		f.expandConnections()
1032	}
1033	
1034	func (f *Fetcher) expandConnections() {
1035		batchSize := f.slowStart.getNextBatchSize()
1036		if batchSize <= 0 {
1037			// Max reached, transition to steady state
1038			f.setState(stateSteady)
1039			// Don't start a new goroutine - let the downloadLoop handle completion
1040			// This avoids multiple goroutines calling wg.Wait() simultaneously
1041			return
1042		}
1043	
1044		totalSize := f.knownSize()
1045	
1046		f.connMu.Lock()
1047	
1048		// For first batch (no existing connections), allocate the remaining file to first connection
1049		if len(f.connections) == 0 {
1050			// Check if we have prefetched data
1051			prefetched := f.resolveDataPos.Load()
1052	
1053			// If prefetched all data, mark as done. A zero size means the extent is
1054			// still unknown, so the first worker must discover it with bytes=start-.
1055			if totalSize > 0 && prefetched >= totalSize {
1056				f.connMu.Unlock()
1057	
1058				// Close the file before signaling completion
1059				f.fileMu.Lock()
1060				if f.file != nil {
1061					f.file.Close()
1062					f.file = nil
1063				}
1064				f.fileMu.Unlock()
1065	
1066				var err error
1067				if chkErr := f.verifyChecksum(); chkErr != nil {
1068					err = chkErr
1069					f.setState(stateError)
1070				} else {
1071					f.setState(stateDone)
1072				}
1073				f.doneCh <- err
1074				return
1075			}
1076	
1077			// First connection starts from prefetched position
1078			connChunk := newOpenEndedChunk(prefetched)
1079			if totalSize > 0 {
1080				connChunk = newChunk(prefetched, totalSize-1)
1081			}
1082			conn := &connection{
1083				ID:    0,
1084				Role:  rolePrimary,
1085				State: connNotStarted,
1086				Chunk: connChunk,
1087			}
1088			// Mark prefetched bytes as already downloaded
1089			conn.Chunk.Downloaded = 0    // Start fresh from prefetched position
1090			conn.Downloaded = prefetched // Track total downloaded including prefetch
1091	
1092			conn.ctx, conn.cancel = context.WithCancel(f.ctx)
1093			f.connections = append(f.connections, conn)
1094			f.connMu.Unlock()
1095	
1096			f.slowStart.commitBatch(1)
1097			f.wg.Add(1)
1098			go f.runConnection(conn)
1099			return
1100		}
1101	
1102		// For subsequent batches, use "help other connection" strategy
1103		// Find connections with enough remaining work to split
1104		// During slow start, use fixed minimum size since speed is not yet stable
1105		minSplitSize := int64(stealMinChunkSize)
1106	
1107		newConns := make([]*connection, 0, batchSize)
1108		for i := 0; i < batchSize; i++ {
1109			// Find the connection with most remaining work
1110			var maxRemainConn *connection
1111			var maxRemain int64
1112	
1113			for _, conn := range f.connections {
1114				if conn.Completed || conn.State == connFailed {
1115					continue
1116				}
1117				if conn.Chunk.openEnded() {
1118					continue
1119				}
1120				remain := conn.Chunk.remain()
1121				// Only split if remaining work is at least 2x the minimum split size
1122				if remain > maxRemain && remain > minSplitSize*2 {
1123					maxRemainConn = conn
1124					maxRemain = remain
1125				}
1126			}
1127	
1128			if maxRemainConn == nil {
1129				// No connection has enough work to split
1130				break
1131			}
1132	
1133			// Split the work: new connection takes the latter half
1134			chunkEnd := *maxRemainConn.Chunk.End
1135			splitPoint := chunkEnd - maxRemainConn.Chunk.remain()/2
1136			newChunk := newChunk(splitPoint+1, chunkEnd)
1137			maxRemainConn.Chunk.setEnd(splitPoint)
1138	
1139			connID := len(f.connections)
1140			conn := &connection{
1141				ID:    connID,
1142				Role:  roleWorker,
1143				State: connNotStarted,
1144				Chunk: newChunk,
1145			}
1146			conn.ctx, conn.cancel = context.WithCancel(f.ctx)
1147	
1148			newConns = append(newConns, conn)
1149			f.connections = append(f.connections, conn)
1150		}
1151	
1152		f.connMu.Unlock()
1153	
1154		if len(newConns) == 0 {
1155			// No new connections could be created, stop expansion
1156			f.setState(stateSteady)
1157			return
1158		}
1159	
1160		// Commit batch to slow start controller
1161		f.slowStart.commitBatch(len(newConns))
1162	
1163		// Launch connections
1164		for _, conn := range newConns {
1165			f.wg.Add(1)
1166			go f.runConnection(conn)
1167		}
1168	}
1169	
1170	func (f *Fetcher) runConnection(conn *connection) {
1171		defer func() {
1172			// A range-advertising origin can fall back to one sequential response.
1173			// Wake the download loop after that connection exits because its earlier
1174			// response-ready signal was intentionally not used to expand.
1175			f.connMu.Lock()
1176			conn.exited = true
1177			sequentialRecovery := !f.meta.Res.Range && (f.rangeReprobeEligible || conn.Completed) && len(f.connections) == 1
1178			f.connMu.Unlock()
1179			f.wg.Done()
1180			if sequentialRecovery && f.slowStart != nil {
1181				f.slowStart.signalExpansion()
1182			}
1183		}()
1184	
1185		f.connMu.Lock()
1186		conn.exited = false
1187		conn.State = connConnecting
1188		f.connMu.Unlock()
1189	
1190		// Use fast-fail client for quick retry during download phase
1191		client := f.buildFastFailClient()
1192		buf := make([]byte, connReadBufferSize)
1193	
1194		retries := 0
1195		f.connMu.Lock()
1196		conn.retryTimes = 0
1197		f.connMu.Unlock()
1198	
1199		for {
1200			// Rebuild client with updated fast-fail timeout on retries
1201			if retries > 0 {
1202				client = f.buildFastFailClient()
1203	
1204				// Preserve an eligible sequential prefix long enough to probe whether
1205				// the origin has recovered byte-range support. downloadChunkOnce resets
1206				// it only when no safe validator exists or If-Range returns a full 200.
1207				f.connMu.Lock()
1208				if !f.hasSequentialPrefixLocked(conn) {
1209					f.resetConnectionForRestart(conn)
1210				}
1211				f.connMu.Unlock()
1212			}
1213	
1214			err := f.downloadChunkOnce(conn, client, buf)
1215			if err == nil {
1216				if !f.meta.Res.Range || !f.helpOtherConnection(conn) {
1217					f.connMu.Lock()
1218					conn.Completed = true
1219					conn.State = connCompleted
1220					f.connMu.Unlock()
1221					return
1222				}
1223	
1224				// Reset counters after a successful help switch
1225				retries = 0
1226				f.connMu.Lock()
1227				conn.retryTimes = 0
1228				f.connMu.Unlock()
1229				continue
1230			}
1231	
1232			if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
1233				return
1234			}
1235			requestErr := extractRequestError(err)
1236			shouldUseResolveFallback := requestErr == nil || !isFailureExemptHTTPCode(requestErr.Code)
1237			if shouldUseResolveFallback && f.completeFromResolveFallback(conn) {
1238				return
1239			}
1240			if isTerminalRangeError(err) {
1241				f.connMu.Lock()
1242				conn.lastErr = err
1243				conn.State = connFailed
1244				conn.failed = true
1245				f.connMu.Unlock()
1246				if f.slowStart != nil {
1247					f.slowStart.onConnectFailed()
1248				}
1249				return
1250			}
1251	
1252			f.connMu.Lock()
1253			if re := extractRequestError(err); re != nil {
1254				conn.lastErr = re
1255			} else {
1256				conn.lastErr = err
1257			}
1258			f.connMu.Unlock()
1259	
1260			if shouldCountHTTPFailure(err) {
1261				if re := extractRequestError(err); re != nil && re.Code == 403 {
1262					f.connMu.Lock()
1263					conn.State = connFailed
1264					conn.failed = true
1265					f.connMu.Unlock()
1266					if f.slowStart != nil {
1267						f.slowStart.onConnectFailed()
1268					}
1269					return
1270				}
1271				f.connMu.Lock()
1272				conn.retryTimes++
1273				retryTimes := conn.retryTimes
1274				conn.failed = true
1275				f.connMu.Unlock()
1276				if f.slowStart != nil {
1277					f.slowStart.onConnectFailed()
1278				}
1279				if retryTimes >= 3 {
1280					f.connMu.Lock()
1281					conn.State = connFailed
1282					f.connMu.Unlock()
1283					return
1284				}
1285			}
1286	
1287			f.connMu.Lock()
1288			conn.State = connFailed
1289			f.connMu.Unlock()
1290			retryDelay := time.Second * time.Duration(retries+1)
1291			if retryDelay > 5*time.Second {
1292				retryDelay = 5 * time.Second
1293			}
1294			retries++
1295			time.Sleep(retryDelay)
1296		}
1297	}
1298	
1299	// downloadChunkOnce performs a single HTTP request for the current chunk without retrying.
1300	// If the redirect URL fails with an expiration-related error (401, 403, 410),
1301	// it will automatically retry with the original URL and update the redirect URL on success.
1302	func (f *Fetcher) downloadChunkOnce(conn *connection, client *http.Client, buf []byte) error {
1303		if conn.ctx.Err() != nil {
1304			return conn.ctx.Err()
1305		}
1306	
1307		// Read chunk boundaries under lock to get a consistent snapshot. A prefix
1308		// without a safe validator cannot be resumed, so restart it before building
1309		// the request; the returned full response will overwrite from byte zero.
1310		f.connMu.Lock()
1311		sequentialSizeUnknown := f.sequentialSizeUnknown
1312		hasSequentialPrefix := f.hasSequentialPrefixLocked(conn)
1313		resumeProbe := f.canProbeSequentialResumeLocked(conn)
1314		intentionalRestart := sequentialSizeUnknown
1315		if sequentialSizeUnknown || (hasSequentialPrefix && !resumeProbe) {
1316			f.resetConnectionForRestart(conn)
1317			f.resolveDataPos.Store(0)
1318			f.rangeValidatorPinned = false
1319			intentionalRestart = true
1320		}
1321		openEndedRange := f.meta.Res.Range && conn.Chunk.openEnded()
1322		if f.meta.Res.Range && !openEndedRange && conn.Chunk.remain() <= 0 {
1323			f.connMu.Unlock()
1324			return nil
1325		}
1326		rangeStart := conn.Chunk.Begin + conn.Chunk.Downloaded
1327		var rangeEnd *int64
1328		if !openEndedRange {
1329			end := *conn.Chunk.End
1330			rangeEnd = &end
1331		}
1332		rangeMode := f.meta.Res.Range
1333		ifRange := ""
1334		if resumeProbe {
1335			end := f.knownSize() - 1
1336			rangeEnd = &end
1337			ifRange = f.ifRange
1338		} else if rangeMode && (f.rangeValidatorPinned || f.resolveFallback.Load()) {
1339			ifRange = f.ifRange
1340		}
1341		f.connMu.Unlock()
1342	
1343		// The read timeout cancels this request through its own context.
1344		reqCtx, reqCancel := context.WithCancel(conn.ctx)
1345		defer reqCancel()
1346	
1347		httpReq, err := f.buildRequest(reqCtx, f.meta.Req)
1348		if err != nil {
1349			return err
1350		}
1351	
1352		if rangeMode || resumeProbe {
1353			httpReq.Header.Set(base.HttpHeaderRange, formatRangeHeader(rangeStart, rangeEnd))

1355				httpReq.Header.Set(base.HttpHeaderIfRange, ifRange)
1356			}
1357		}
1358		rangeRequested := httpReq.Header.Get(base.HttpHeaderRange) != ""
1359	
1360		// Record connection start time for adaptive timeout tracking
1361		connStartTime := time.Now()
1362	
1363		resp, err := client.Do(httpReq)
1364		if err != nil {
1365			return err
1366		}
1367	
1368		if resp.StatusCode != base.HttpCodeOK && resp.StatusCode != base.HttpCodePartialContent {
1369			resp.Body.Close()
1370			originalErr := NewRequestError(resp.StatusCode)
1371	
1372			// Check if this might be a redirect URL expiration error
1373			// If so, try falling back to the original URL
1374			if f.hasRedirectURL() && isRedirectExpiredError(originalErr) {
1375				fallbackResp, fallbackErr := f.tryFallbackToOriginalURL(reqCtx, client, rangeStart, rangeEnd, rangeRequested, ifRange)
1376				if fallbackErr == nil && fallbackResp != nil {
1377					// Fallback succeeded, use this response instead
1378					resp = fallbackResp
1379					// Update the redirect URL from the response
1380					if resp.Request != nil && resp.Request.URL != nil {
1381						f.updateRedirectURL(resp.Request.URL.String())
1382					}
1383				} else {
1384					// Fallback also failed, return the original error
1385					if fallbackResp != nil {
1386						fallbackResp.Body.Close()
1387					}
1388					return originalErr
1389				}
1390			} else {
1391				return originalErr
1392			}
1393		}
1394	
1395		expectedResponseLength := int64(-1)
1396		var responseBytesToDiscard int64
1397		if rangeRequested && resp.StatusCode == base.HttpCodeOK {
1398			if conn.ID == 0 && f.resolveFallback.CompareAndSwap(true, false) {
1399				// This response is itself a complete representation, so the older
1400				// Resolve stream is no longer needed. Stop and copy its prefix before
1401				// the sequential restart truncates/overwrites the target from zero.
1402				f.stopPrefetchAndCopyData()
1403			}
1404			if resumeProbe {
1405				// If-Range returning 200 provides the complete current representation.
1406				// Discard the old prefix counters and consume this response from byte 0.
1407				f.restartSequentialDownload(conn, extractIfRangeValidator(resp.Header))
1408				intentionalRestart = true
1409			} else {
1410				if err := f.fallbackToSequentialDownload(conn, extractIfRangeValidator(resp.Header)); err != nil {
1411					resp.Body.Close()
1412					return fmt.Errorf("%w: expected 206 Partial Content, got 200 OK", err)
1413				}
1414				intentionalRestart = true
1415			}
1416		}
1417		if rangeRequested && resp.StatusCode == base.HttpCodePartialContent {
1418			var responseTotal int64
1419			expectedResponseLength, responseTotal, err = validateRangeResponse(resp, rangeStart, rangeEnd, f.knownSize())
1420			if err != nil {
1421				resp.Body.Close()
1422				return err
1423			}
1424			if openEndedRange {
1425				if err := f.resolveOpenEndedRange(conn, responseTotal); err != nil {
1426					resp.Body.Close()
1427					return err
1428				}
1429			}
1430			responseBytesToDiscard, err = f.commitResolveTakeover(conn, rangeStart)
1431			if err != nil {
1432				resp.Body.Close()
1433				return err
1434			}
1435			if resumeProbe {
1436				// The origin recovered Range support. Convert the preserved sequential
1437				// prefix into a normal ranged chunk before writing the suffix.
1438				f.connMu.Lock()
1439				f.meta.Res.Range = true
1440				f.rangeReprobeEligible = false
1441				f.rangeValidatorPinned = true
1442				f.sequentialSizeUnknown = false
1443				conn.Chunk.Begin = 0
1444				conn.Chunk.setEnd(f.knownSize() - 1)
1445				f.connMu.Unlock()
1446			}
1447		}
1448		if !rangeRequested && resp.StatusCode == base.HttpCodeOK {
1449			f.connMu.Lock()
1450			if f.rangeReprobeEligible {
1451				// This full response might itself become the retained prefix if its
1452				// body is interrupted, so bind any later If-Range probe to it.
1453				f.ifRange = extractIfRangeValidator(resp.Header)
1454			}
1455			f.connMu.Unlock()
1456		}
1457		if !f.meta.Res.Range && resp.StatusCode == base.HttpCodeOK {
1458			if intentionalRestart {
1459				if resp.ContentLength >= 0 {
1460					if err := f.resizeSequentialResource(resp.ContentLength); err != nil {
1461						resp.Body.Close()
1462						return err
1463					}
1464					expectedResponseLength = resp.ContentLength
1465				} else if err := f.beginUnknownSizeSequentialResource(); err != nil {
1466					resp.Body.Close()
1467					return err
1468				}
1469			} else if f.hasKnownSize() && f.meta.Res.Size > 0 {
1470				expectedResponseLength = f.meta.Res.Size
1471				if resp.ContentLength >= 0 && resp.ContentLength != expectedResponseLength {
1472					resp.Body.Close()
1473					return fmt.Errorf("%w: Content-Length %d does not match resource size %d", errInvalidRangeResponse, resp.ContentLength, expectedResponseLength)
1474				}
1475			}
1476		}
1477		defer resp.Body.Close()
1478	
1479		// Record successful connection time for adaptive timeout
1480		f.updateMaxConnTime(time.Since(connStartTime))
1481	
1482		f.connMu.Lock()
1483		conn.State = connDownloading
1484		conn.failed = false
1485		f.connMu.Unlock()
1486	
1487		if conn.Role == rolePrimary || conn.ID == 0 {
1488			f.primaryReadyOnce.Do(func() {
1489				close(f.primaryReadyCh)
1490			})
1491		}
1492		if f.slowStart != nil {
1493			f.slowStart.onConnectSuccess()
1494		}
1495	
1496		reader := f.responseReader(resp, reqCancel)
1497		var responseBytesRead int64
1498		for {
1499			if conn.ctx.Err() != nil {
1500				return conn.ctx.Err()
1501			}
1502	
1503			n, err := reader.Read(buf)
1504			if n > 0 {
1505				responseBytesRead += int64(n)
1506				if expectedResponseLength >= 0 && responseBytesRead > expectedResponseLength {
1507					return fmt.Errorf("%w: response body exceeds expected length %d", errInvalidRangeResponse, expectedResponseLength)
1508				}
1509	
1510				data := buf[:n]
1511				if responseBytesToDiscard > 0 {
1512					discard := min(int64(len(data)), responseBytesToDiscard)
1513					data = data[discard:]
1514					responseBytesToDiscard -= discard
1515				}
1516	
1517				finished := false
1518				var writeOffset int64
1519	
1520				if len(data) > 0 {
1521					// Lock to safely read chunk state and calculate write parameters
1522					// This protects against concurrent chunk splitting by helpOtherConnection
1523					f.connMu.Lock()
1524					if f.meta.Res.Range {
1525						// Check current chunk boundaries - this respects any concurrent chunk splitting
1526						remain := conn.Chunk.remain()
1527						if remain <= 0 {
1528							// Chunk has been fully downloaded (possibly split and reduced)
1529							f.connMu.Unlock()
1530							return nil
1531						}
1532						if remain < int64(len(data)) {
1533							data = data[:remain]
1534							finished = true
1535						}
1536					}
1537					writeOffset = conn.Chunk.Begin + conn.Chunk.Downloaded
1538					f.connMu.Unlock()
1539	
1540					f.fileMu.Lock()
1541					if f.file != nil {
1542						_, writeErr := f.file.WriteAt(data, writeOffset)
1543						if writeErr != nil {
1544							f.fileMu.Unlock()
1545							return writeErr
1546						}
1547					}
1548					f.fileMu.Unlock()
1549	
1550					// Lock again to update Downloaded atomically with the read above
1551					f.connMu.Lock()
1552					conn.Chunk.Downloaded += int64(len(data))
1553					conn.Downloaded += int64(len(data))
1554					// Update connection speed periodically
1555					now := time.Now().UnixNano()
1556					if conn.lastSpeedCheck == 0 {
1557						conn.lastSpeedCheck = now
1558						conn.lastSpeedDownload = conn.Downloaded
1559					} else if now-conn.lastSpeedCheck >= int64(500*time.Millisecond) {
1560						elapsed := float64(now-conn.lastSpeedCheck) / float64(time.Second)
1561						if elapsed > 0 {
1562							conn.speed = int64(float64(conn.Downloaded-conn.lastSpeedDownload) / elapsed)
1563						}
1564						conn.lastSpeedCheck = now
1565						conn.lastSpeedDownload = conn.Downloaded
1566					}
1567					f.connMu.Unlock()
1568	
1569					if finished {
1570						return nil
1571					}
1572				}
1573			}
1574	
1575			if err != nil {
1576				if err == io.EOF {
1577					if intentionalRestart && resp.ContentLength < 0 {
1578						if err := f.resizeSequentialResource(responseBytesRead); err != nil {
1579							return err
1580						}
1581					}
1582					if expectedResponseLength >= 0 && responseBytesRead != expectedResponseLength {
1583						if rangeRequested && responseBytesRead < expectedResponseLength {
1584							return fmt.Errorf("%w: response body length %d, expected %d", errIncompleteResponse, responseBytesRead, expectedResponseLength)
1585						}
1586						return fmt.Errorf("%w: response body length %d, expected %d", errInvalidRangeResponse, responseBytesRead, expectedResponseLength)
1587					}
1588					return nil
1589				}
1590				return err
1591			}
1592		}
1593	}

1595	// commitResolveTakeover stops the still-live Resolve download only after the
1596	// first Range response has been validated. Resolve may have advanced beyond
1597	// requestedStart while the speculative request was in flight, so the overlap
1598	// is returned for the caller to discard from the Range response body.
1599	func (f *Fetcher) commitResolveTakeover(conn *connection, requestedStart int64) (int64, error) {
1600		if conn.ID != 0 || !f.resolveFallback.CompareAndSwap(true, false) {
1601			return 0, nil
1602		}
1603	
1604		prefetched := f.stopPrefetchAndCopyData()
1605		if prefetched < requestedStart || prefetched > f.knownSize() {
1606			return 0, fmt.Errorf("resolve prefetch advanced to invalid offset %d for range start %d", prefetched, requestedStart)
1607		}
1608		f.resolveDataPos.Store(prefetched)
1609	
1610		overlap := prefetched - requestedStart
1611		f.connMu.Lock()
1612		if f.ifRange != "" {
1613			f.rangeValidatorPinned = true
1614		}
1615		conn.Chunk.Downloaded = overlap
1616		conn.Downloaded = prefetched
1617		f.connMu.Unlock()
1618		return overlap, nil
1619	}

1621	// completeFromResolveFallback keeps the original full response authoritative
1622	// when the speculative first Range request cannot take over. It waits for that
1623	// response to finish, copies it once, and converts the task to one completed
1624	// sequential connection instead of accepting an incomplete Range result.
1625	func (f *Fetcher) completeFromResolveFallback(conn *connection) bool {
1626		if conn.ID != 0 || !f.resolveFallback.CompareAndSwap(true, false) {
1627			return false
1628		}
1629	
1630		for !f.prefetchDone.Load() {
1631			if conn.ctx.Err() != nil {
1632				return false
1633			}
1634			time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
1635		}
1636		knownSize := f.hasKnownSize()
1637		if f.prefetchErr != nil || (knownSize && f.prefetchSize.Load() != f.meta.Res.Size) {
1638			f.cleanupPrefetchFile()
1639			return false
1640		}
1641	
1642		prefetched := f.stopPrefetchAndCopyData()
1643		if knownSize && prefetched != f.meta.Res.Size {
1644			return false
1645		}
1646		f.resolveDataPos.Store(prefetched)
1647	
1648		f.connMu.Lock()
1649		if !knownSize {
1650			f.setResourceSizeLocked(prefetched, true)
1651		}
1652		f.meta.Res.Range = false
1653		f.rangeReprobeEligible = false
1654		f.rangeValidatorPinned = false
1655		conn.Chunk = newChunk(0, prefetched-1)
1656		conn.Chunk.Downloaded = prefetched
1657		conn.Downloaded = prefetched
1658		conn.Completed = true
1659		conn.State = connCompleted
1660		conn.failed = false
1661		conn.lastErr = nil
1662		f.connMu.Unlock()
1663		return true
1664	}

1666	// parseRangeResponse validates a single byte range with a known complete length.
1667	// Unknown totals are rejected: a segment length cannot stand in for resource size.
1668	func parseRangeResponse(resp *http.Response) (int64, int64, int64, error) {
1669		contentRange := resp.Header.Get(base.HttpHeaderContentRange)
1670		fields := strings.Fields(contentRange)
1671		if len(fields) != 2 || !strings.EqualFold(fields[0], base.HttpHeaderBytes) {
1672			return 0, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("%w: malformed Content-Range %q", errInvalidRangeResponse, contentRange)
1673		}
1674	
1675		rangeAndTotal := strings.Split(fields[1], "/")
1676		if len(rangeAndTotal) != 2 {
1677			return 0, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("%w: malformed Content-Range %q", errInvalidRangeResponse, contentRange)
1678		}
1679		bounds := strings.Split(rangeAndTotal[0], "-")
1680		if len(bounds) != 2 {
1681			return 0, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("%w: malformed Content-Range %q", errInvalidRangeResponse, contentRange)
1682		}
1683	
1684		start, startErr := strconv.ParseInt(bounds[0], 10, 64)
1685		end, endErr := strconv.ParseInt(bounds[1], 10, 64)
1686		total, totalErr := strconv.ParseInt(rangeAndTotal[1], 10, 64)
1687		if startErr != nil || endErr != nil || totalErr != nil || start < 0 || end < start || total <= end {
1688			return 0, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("%w: malformed Content-Range %q", errInvalidRangeResponse, contentRange)
1689		}
1690		expectedLength := end - start + 1
1691		if resp.ContentLength >= 0 && resp.ContentLength != expectedLength {
1692			return 0, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("%w: Content-Length %d does not match range length %d", errInvalidRangeResponse, resp.ContentLength, expectedLength)
1693		}
1694		return start, end, total, nil
1695	}
1696	
1697	func validateRangeResponse(resp *http.Response, requestedStart int64, requestedEnd *int64, totalSize int64) (int64, int64, error) {
1698		start, end, total, err := parseRangeResponse(resp)
1699		if err != nil {
1700			return 0, 0, err
1701		}
1702		if start != requestedStart || (requestedEnd != nil && end != *requestedEnd) || (requestedEnd == nil && end != total-1) {
1703			return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("%w: Content-Range %d-%d does not match requested range", errInvalidRangeResponse, start, end)
1704		}
1705		if totalSize > 0 && total != totalSize {
1706			return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("%w: Content-Range total %d does not match resource size %d", errInvalidRangeResponse, total, totalSize)
1707		}
1708	
1709		return end - start + 1, total, nil
1710	}

1712	func (f *Fetcher) resolveOpenEndedRange(conn *connection, totalSize int64) error {
1713		if totalSize <= 0 {
1714			return fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid discovered resource size %d", errInvalidRangeResponse, totalSize)
1715		}
1716	
1717		// Publish the discovered extent before the response-ready signal can expand
1718		// the slow-start batch. Store observes the same metadata/progress snapshot.
1719		f.connMu.Lock()
1720		f.fileMu.Lock()
1721		if f.file == nil {
1722			f.fileMu.Unlock()
1723			f.connMu.Unlock()
1724			return errors.New("target file is not open")
1725		}
1726		err := f.file.Truncate(totalSize)
1727		f.fileMu.Unlock()
1728		if err != nil {
1729			f.connMu.Unlock()
1730			return err
1731		}
1732		f.setResourceSizeLocked(totalSize, true)
1733		conn.Chunk.setEnd(totalSize - 1)
1734		f.connMu.Unlock()
1735		return nil
1736	}

1738	// fallbackToSequentialDownload handles origins that advertise byte ranges but
1739	// ignore the first Range request and return the full representation with 200.
1740	// Slow start launches only the primary connection initially, so it is safe to
1741	// reset the prefetch offset and consume that response from byte zero. If the
1742	// server changes behavior after parallel connections have started, fail rather
1743	// than risk assembling a corrupt file.
1744	func (f *Fetcher) fallbackToSequentialDownload(conn *connection, ifRange string) error {
1745		f.connMu.Lock()
1746		defer f.connMu.Unlock()
1747	
1748		if !f.meta.Res.Range {
1749			return nil
1750		}
1751		if conn.ID != 0 || len(f.connections) != 1 {
1752			return errRangeRequestIgnored
1753		}
1754	
1755		f.meta.Res.Range = false
1756		f.rangeReprobeEligible = true
1757		f.rangeValidatorPinned = false
1758		f.ifRange = ifRange
1759		f.resetConnectionForRestart(conn)
1760		f.resolveDataPos.Store(0)
1761		return nil
1762	}
1763	
1764	// restartSequentialDownload consumes an If-Range 200 response as the complete
1765	// current representation. The old prefix is no longer trusted, but this body
1766	// can safely overwrite it from byte zero.
1767	func (f *Fetcher) restartSequentialDownload(conn *connection, ifRange string) {
1768		f.connMu.Lock()
1769		defer f.connMu.Unlock()
1770	
1771		f.meta.Res.Range = false
1772		f.rangeReprobeEligible = true
1773		f.rangeValidatorPinned = false
1774		f.ifRange = ifRange
1775		f.resetConnectionForRestart(conn)
1776		f.resolveDataPos.Store(0)
1777	}
1778	
1779	// resizeSequentialResource makes a full restart response authoritative for
1780	// both progress accounting and the target file. Truncation removes stale tail
1781	// bytes when the new representation is shorter and preallocates when longer.
1782	func (f *Fetcher) resizeSequentialResource(size int64) error {
1783		if size < 0 {
1784			return fmt.Errorf("invalid sequential response size %d", size)
1785		}
1786	
1787		// Keep the file mutation and its recovery metadata in one connMu critical
1788		// section so Store cannot persist one side of the transition without the
1789		// other. Other download paths never hold fileMu while acquiring connMu.
1790		f.connMu.Lock()
1791		f.fileMu.Lock()
1792		if f.file == nil {
1793			f.fileMu.Unlock()
1794			f.connMu.Unlock()
1795			return errors.New("target file is not open")
1796		}
1797		err := f.file.Truncate(size)
1798		f.fileMu.Unlock()
1799		if err != nil {
1800			f.connMu.Unlock()
1801			return err
1802		}
1803	
1804		f.setResourceSizeLocked(size, true)
1805		f.sequentialSizeUnknown = false
1806		f.connMu.Unlock()
1807		return nil
1808	}
1809	
1810	// beginUnknownSizeSequentialResource discards all stale bytes and records that
1811	// a restarted chunked response has no authoritative total size yet. If this
1812	// response is interrupted, the persisted flag forces the next attempt to start
1813	// from byte zero instead of validating a Range response against an old size.
1814	func (f *Fetcher) beginUnknownSizeSequentialResource() error {
1815		f.connMu.Lock()
1816		f.fileMu.Lock()
1817		if f.file == nil {
1818			f.fileMu.Unlock()
1819			f.connMu.Unlock()
1820			return errors.New("target file is not open")
1821		}
1822		err := f.file.Truncate(0)
1823		f.fileMu.Unlock()
1824		if err != nil {
1825			f.connMu.Unlock()
1826			return err
1827		}
1828	
1829		f.setResourceSizeLocked(0, false)
1830		f.sequentialSizeUnknown = true
1831		f.ifRange = ""
1832		f.rangeValidatorPinned = false
1833		f.connMu.Unlock()
1834		return nil
1835	}

1837	// runConnectionWithResolveResp uses the response body from Resolve phase
1838	// This is crucial for one-time URLs that can only be accessed once
1839	func (f *Fetcher) runConnectionWithResolveResp(conn *connection) {
1840		defer f.wg.Done()
1841	
1842		f.connMu.Lock()
1843		conn.State = connConnecting
1844		f.connMu.Unlock()
1845	
1846		buf := make([]byte, connReadBufferSize)
1847	
1848		// Get the resolve response
1849		f.resolveRespLock.Lock()
1850		resp, cancel := f.resolveResp, f.resolveRespCancel
1851		f.resolveResp, f.resolveRespCancel = nil, nil // Take ownership
1852		f.resolveRespLock.Unlock()
1853	
1854		if resp == nil {
1855			// No resolve response available, fall back to normal connection
1856			f.runConnectionFallback(conn)
1857			return
1858		}
1859	
1860		if cancel != nil {
1861			defer cancel()
1862		}
1863		defer resp.Body.Close()
1864	
1865		f.connMu.Lock()
1866		conn.State = connDownloading
1867		conn.failed = false
1868		f.connMu.Unlock()
1869	
1870		// Signal primary ready
1871		f.primaryReadyOnce.Do(func() {
1872			close(f.primaryReadyCh)
1873		})
1874		if f.slowStart != nil {
1875			f.slowStart.onConnectSuccess()
1876		}
1877	
1878		// Download data from resolve response
1879		reader := f.responseReader(resp, cancel)
1880		for {
1881			if conn.ctx.Err() != nil {
1882				return
1883			}
1884	
1885			n, err := reader.Read(buf)
1886			if n > 0 {
1887				f.connMu.Lock()
1888				writeOffset := conn.Chunk.Downloaded
1889				f.connMu.Unlock()
1890	
1891				f.fileMu.Lock()
1892				if f.file != nil {
1893					_, writeErr := f.file.WriteAt(buf[:n], writeOffset)
1894					if writeErr != nil {
1895						f.fileMu.Unlock()
1896						f.connMu.Lock()
1897						conn.State = connFailed
1898						conn.failed = true
1899						f.connMu.Unlock()
1900						if f.slowStart != nil {
1901							f.slowStart.onConnectFailed()
1902						}
1903						return
1904					}
1905				}
1906				f.fileMu.Unlock()
1907	
1908				f.connMu.Lock()
1909				conn.Chunk.Downloaded += int64(n)
1910				conn.Downloaded += int64(n)
1911				f.connMu.Unlock()
1912			}
1913			if err != nil {
1914				if err == io.EOF {
1915					f.connMu.Lock()
1916					if !f.hasKnownSize() {
1917						f.setResourceSizeLocked(conn.Downloaded, true)

1937	// runConnectionFallback is used when resolve response is not available
1938	func (f *Fetcher) runConnectionFallback(conn *connection) {
1939		// Use fast-fail client for quick retry during download phase
1940		client := f.buildFastFailClient()
1941		buf := make([]byte, connReadBufferSize)
1942	
1943		retries := 0
1944		countedRetries := 0
1945	
1946		for {
1947			if conn.ctx.Err() != nil {
1948				return
1949			}
1950	
1951			// Rebuild client with updated fast-fail timeout on retries
1952			if retries > 0 {
1953				client = f.buildFastFailClient()
1954			}
1955	
1956			f.connMu.Lock()
1957			if retries > 0 {
1958				f.resetConnectionForRestart(conn)
1959			}
1960			conn.State = connConnecting
1961			f.connMu.Unlock()
1962	
1963			// Restored tasks without a reusable Resolve response need the same
1964			// length handling and restart semantics as other sequential requests.
1965			err := f.downloadChunkOnce(conn, client, buf)
1966	
1967			if err == nil {
1968				f.connMu.Lock()
1969				conn.Completed = true
1970				conn.State = connCompleted
1971				f.connMu.Unlock()
1972				return
1973			}
1974	
1975			if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
1976				return
1977			}
1978	
1979			f.connMu.Lock()
1980			if re := extractRequestError(err); re != nil {
1981				conn.lastErr = re
1982			} else {
1983				conn.lastErr = err
1984			}
1985			f.connMu.Unlock()
1986	
1987			if shouldCountHTTPFailure(err) {
1988				// Immediate fail for server connection limit (403)
1989				if re := extractRequestError(err); re != nil && re.Code == 403 {
1990					f.connMu.Lock()
1991					conn.State = connFailed
1992					conn.failed = true
1993					f.connMu.Unlock()
1994					if f.slowStart != nil {
1995						f.slowStart.onConnectFailed()
1996					}
1997					return
1998				}
1999				f.connMu.Lock()
2000				conn.retryTimes++
2001				f.connMu.Unlock()
2002				countedRetries++
2003				if countedRetries >= 3 {
2004					f.connMu.Lock()
2005					conn.State = connFailed
2006					conn.failed = true
2007					f.connMu.Unlock()
2008					if f.slowStart != nil {
2009						f.slowStart.onConnectFailed()
2010					}
2011					return
2012				}
2013				// Retry again for counted failures below the cap
2014				f.connMu.Lock()
2015				conn.State = connFailed
2016				f.connMu.Unlock()
2017				retryDelay := time.Second * time.Duration(retries+1)
2018				if retryDelay > 5*time.Second {
2019					retryDelay = 5 * time.Second
2020				}
2021				retries++
2022				time.Sleep(retryDelay)
2023				continue
2024			}
2025	
2026			// Retry indefinitely for non-counted errors
2027			f.connMu.Lock()
2028			conn.State = connFailed
2029			f.connMu.Unlock()
2030			retryDelay := time.Second * time.Duration(retries+1)
2031			if retryDelay > 5*time.Second {
2032				retryDelay = 5 * time.Second
2033			}
2034			retries++
2035			time.Sleep(retryDelay)
2036		}
2037	}

2039	// helpOtherConnection implements work stealing: when a connection finishes its chunk,
2040	// it looks for connections that need more than stealThresholdSeconds to finish and steals half of its work.
2041	func (f *Fetcher) helpOtherConnection(helper *connection) bool {
2042		f.connMu.Lock()
2043		defer f.connMu.Unlock()
2044	
2045		// Find the connection with longest remaining time
2046		var slowestConn *connection
2047		var maxRemainSeconds int64
2048		for _, r := range f.connections {
2049			if r == helper || r.Completed || r.State == connFailed {
2050				continue
2051			}
2052			if r.Chunk.openEnded() {
2053				continue
2054			}
2055	
2056			remain := r.Chunk.remain()
2057			if remain < stealMinChunkSize {
2058				continue
2059			}
2060	
2061			// Calculate remaining time in seconds for this connection
2062			var remainSeconds int64
2063			if r.speed > 0 {
2064				remainSeconds = remain / r.speed
2065			} else {
2066				// Speed unknown, assume it needs help if chunk is large enough
2067				remainSeconds = stealThresholdSeconds + 1
2068			}
2069	
2070			// Only consider if it needs more than threshold seconds to finish
2071			if remainSeconds > stealThresholdSeconds && remainSeconds > maxRemainSeconds {
2072				slowestConn = r
2073				maxRemainSeconds = remainSeconds
2074			}
2075		}
2076	
2077		if slowestConn == nil {
2078			return false
2079		}
2080	
2081		// Re-calculate the chunk range: steal half of the remaining work
2082		chunkEnd := *slowestConn.Chunk.End
2083		helper.Chunk.Begin = chunkEnd - slowestConn.Chunk.remain()/2
2084		helper.Chunk.setEnd(chunkEnd)
2085		helper.Chunk.Downloaded = 0
2086		slowestConn.Chunk.setEnd(helper.Chunk.Begin - 1)
2087		return true
2088	}

2139	func (f *Fetcher) resumeConnections() {
2140		// Collect connections to resume while holding the lock
2141		var toResume []*connection
2142	
2143		f.connMu.Lock()
2144		for _, conn := range f.connections {
2145			// Only skip connections that have truly completed successfully
2146			if conn.Completed || conn.State == connCompleted {
2147				continue
2148			}
2149			// For failed connections, skip if:
2150			// 1. They have exhausted retries (retryTimes >= 3), OR
2151			// 2. They failed with a permanent error like 403
2152			if conn.State == connFailed && conn.failed {
2153				// Check if it's a permanent error (like 403)
2154				if re := extractRequestError(conn.lastErr); re != nil && re.Code == 403 {
2155					continue
2156				}
2157				// Check if retries exhausted
2158				if conn.retryTimes >= 3 {
2159					continue
2160				}
2161			}
2162			if !f.hasSequentialPrefixLocked(conn) {
2163				f.resetConnectionForRestart(conn)
2164			}
2165			// Reset the connection state for resume
2166			conn.ctx, conn.cancel = context.WithCancel(f.ctx)
2167			conn.State = connNotStarted
2168			conn.failed = false // Clear failed flag for resumed connection
2169			toResume = append(toResume, conn)
2170		}
2171		f.connMu.Unlock()
2172	
2173		// Start connections outside the lock
2174		for _, conn := range toResume {
2175			f.wg.Add(1)
2176			go f.runConnection(conn)
2177		}
2178	}

2188	func (f *Fetcher) onDownloadComplete() {
2189		f.connMu.Lock()
2190	
2191		// First, check if download actually completed successfully
2192		// Calculate total downloaded from all connections
2193		totalDownloaded := int64(0)
2194		if f.resolveConn != nil {
2195			totalDownloaded += f.resolveConn.Downloaded
2196		}
2197		for _, conn := range f.connections {
2198			totalDownloaded += conn.Downloaded
2199		}
2200	
2201		// Check if all chunks are complete (no remaining bytes)
2202		allChunksComplete := true
2203		for _, conn := range f.connections {
2204			needsMoreData := false
2205			if f.meta.Res.Range {
2206				needsMoreData = conn.Chunk != nil && (conn.Chunk.openEnded() || conn.Chunk.remain() > 0)
2207			} else if f.hasKnownSize() && f.meta.Res.Size > 0 {
2208				needsMoreData = conn.Downloaded < f.meta.Res.Size
2209			} else {
2210				needsMoreData = !conn.Completed && conn.State != connCompleted
2211			}
2212	
2213			if needsMoreData && !conn.Completed && conn.State != connCompleted {
2214				// This connection has remaining work and isn't done
2215				// Check if it failed with 403 (server limit) - these can be ignored if other connections completed the work
2216				if conn.State == connFailed && conn.failed {
2217					if re := extractRequestError(conn.lastErr); re != nil && re.Code == 403 && f.hasKnownSize() {
2218						// 403 is server connection limit, check if other connections will complete this chunk
2219						continue
2220					}
2221				}
2222				allChunksComplete = false
2223				break
2224			}
2225		}
2226	
2227		// If total downloaded matches file size, consider it a success regardless of connection failures
2228		downloadComplete := f.hasKnownSize() && f.meta.Res.Size > 0 && totalDownloaded >= f.meta.Res.Size
2229	
2230		// Integrity errors must win over byte-count completion. A malformed response
2231		// may be detected only after the expected bytes have already been written.
2232		var finalErr error
2233		for _, conn := range f.connections {
2234			if conn.State == connFailed && conn.failed && isTerminalRangeError(conn.lastErr) {
2235				finalErr = fmt.Errorf("connection %d failed: retries=%d, err=%w", conn.ID, conn.retryTimes, conn.lastErr)
2236				break
2237			}
2238		}
2239	
2240		// Check for other errors, but ignore 403 (server connection limit) errors if download completed.
2241		if finalErr == nil && !downloadComplete && !allChunksComplete {
2242			for _, conn := range f.connections {
2243				if conn.State == connFailed && conn.failed {
2244					// Skip 403 errors (server connection limit) - these are expected when exceeding server's limit
2245					if re := extractRequestError(conn.lastErr); re != nil && re.Code == 403 && f.hasKnownSize() {
2246						continue
2247					}
2248					if re := extractRequestError(conn.lastErr); re != nil {
2249						finalErr = fmt.Errorf("connection %d failed: retries=%d, status=%d", conn.ID, conn.retryTimes, re.Code)
2250					} else if conn.lastErr != nil {
2251						finalErr = fmt.Errorf("connection %d failed: retries=%d, err=%v", conn.ID, conn.retryTimes, conn.lastErr)
2252					} else {
2253						finalErr = fmt.Errorf("connection %d failed: retries=%d", conn.ID, conn.retryTimes)
2254					}
2255					break
2256				}
2257			}
2258		}
2259		f.connMu.Unlock()
2260	
2261		// Close the file before signaling completion
2262		// This ensures the file handle is released before Wait() returns
2263		f.fileMu.Lock()
2264		if f.file != nil {
2265			f.file.Close()
2266			f.file = nil
2267		}
2268		f.fileMu.Unlock()
2269	
2270		if finalErr == nil {
2271			if chkErr := f.verifyChecksum(); chkErr != nil {
2272				finalErr = chkErr
2273				f.setState(stateError)
2274			} else {
2275				f.setState(stateDone)
2276			}
2277		} else {
2278			f.setState(stateError)
2279		}
2280	
2281		select {
2282		case f.doneCh <- finalErr:
2283		default:
2284		}
2285	}

2287	func (f *Fetcher) verifyChecksum() error {
2288		if f.meta == nil || f.meta.Opts == nil || f.meta.Opts.Extra == nil {
2289			return nil
2290		}
2291		extra, ok := f.meta.Opts.Extra.(*fhttp.OptsExtra)
2292		if !ok || extra.Checksum == nil {
2293			return nil
2294		}
2295		chk := extra.Checksum
2296		if chk.Algorithm == "" && chk.Expected == "" {
2297			return nil
2298		}
2299		var h hash.Hash
2300		switch strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(chk.Algorithm)) {
2301		case "md5":
2302			h = md5.New()
2303		case "sha1", "sha-1":
2304			h = sha1.New()
2305		case "sha256", "sha-256":
2306			h = sha256.New()
2307		default:
2308			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported checksum algorithm: %s", chk.Algorithm)
2309		}
2310	
2311		filePath := f.meta.SingleFilepath()
2312		file, err := os.Open(filePath)
2313		if err != nil {
2314			return fmt.Errorf("open file for checksum verification failed: %w", err)
2315		}
2316		defer file.Close()
2317	
2318		buf := make([]byte, 64*1024)
2319		if _, err := io.CopyBuffer(h, file, buf); err != nil {
2320			return fmt.Errorf("calculate checksum failed: %w", err)
2321		}
2322	
2323		actual := hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil))
2324		expected := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(chk.Expected))
2325		if !strings.EqualFold(actual, expected) {
2326			f.checksumFailed.Store(true)
2327			return fmt.Errorf("checksum mismatch: expected %s, got %s", expected, actual)
2328		}
2329		return nil
2330	}

2332	func (f *Fetcher) checkCompletion() bool {
2333		// Check if all data has been downloaded
2334		f.connMu.Lock()
2335		defer f.connMu.Unlock()
2336	
2337		totalDownloaded := int64(0)
2338		if f.resolveConn != nil {
2339			totalDownloaded += f.resolveConn.Downloaded
2340		}
2341		for _, conn := range f.connections {

2343		}

2345		if f.hasKnownSize() && f.meta.Res.Size > 0 && totalDownloaded >= f.meta.Res.Size {

2347			return true
2348		}

2398				if patchExtra.Method != "" {
2399					existingExtra.Method = patchExtra.Method
2400				}
2401				// Update Body only if non-empty
2402				if patchExtra.Body != "" {
2403					existingExtra.Body = patchExtra.Body
2404				}
2405				// Merge Headers: existing keys are overwritten, new keys are added
2406				if patchExtra.Header != nil {
2407					if existingExtra.Header == nil {
2408						existingExtra.Header = make(map[string]string)
2409					}
2410					for k, v := range patchExtra.Header {
2411						existingExtra.Header[k] = v
2412					}
2413				}
2414			}
2415			// Merge Labels: existing keys are overwritten, new keys are added
2416			if req.Labels != nil {
2417				if f.meta.Req.Labels == nil {
2418					f.meta.Req.Labels = make(map[string]string)
2419				}
2420				for k, v := range req.Labels {

2422				}
2423			}
2424			if req.Proxy != nil {

2426			}
2427		}

2429		return nil
2430	}

2432	func (f *Fetcher) Pause() error {
2433		if f.cancel != nil {
2434			f.cancel()
2435		}
2436		if f.resolveCancel != nil {
2437			f.resolveCancel()
2438		}
2439	
2440		// Stop prefetch if running
2441		if f.prefetchStopCh != nil {
2442			select {
2443			case <-f.prefetchStopCh:
2444				// Already closed
2445			default:
2446				close(f.prefetchStopCh)
2447			}
2448		}
2449	
2450		// Wait for downloadLoop to exit first (it will call wg.Wait internally)
2451		if f.downloadLoopDone != nil {
2452			<-f.downloadLoopDone
2453		}
2454	
2455		// Wait for all connection goroutines to stop
2456		f.wg.Wait()
2457	
2458		// Wait for prefetch to finish
2459		for f.prefetchStopCh != nil && !f.prefetchDone.Load() {
2460			time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
2461		}
2462	
2463		// If Pause wins before the first Range response is validated, materialize
2464		// the Resolve prefix before discarding its temporary file. The first
2465		// connection was allocated after the earlier prefetch snapshot, so advance
2466		// its range start to the final copied offset for a safe persisted resume.
2467		if f.meta != nil && f.meta.Res != nil && f.meta.Res.Range && f.prefetchFile != nil {
2468			f.resolveFallback.Store(false)
2469			prefetched := f.stopPrefetchAndCopyData()
2470			if prefetched > 0 {
2471				f.resolveDataPos.Store(prefetched)
2472				f.connMu.Lock()
2473				if len(f.connections) == 1 {
2474					conn := f.connections[0]
2475					if conn != nil && conn.ID == 0 && conn.Chunk != nil && !conn.Completed {
2476						conn.Chunk.Begin = prefetched
2477						if f.knownSize() > 0 {
2478							conn.Chunk.setEnd(f.knownSize() - 1)
2479						} else {
2480							conn.Chunk.End = nil
2481						}
2482						conn.Chunk.Downloaded = 0
2483						conn.Downloaded = prefetched
2484					}
2485				}
2486				f.connMu.Unlock()
2487			}
2488		} else {
2489			f.cleanupPrefetchFile()
2490		}
2491	
2492		// Clean up resolve response if still held
2493		f.resolveRespLock.Lock()
2494		f.closeResolveRespLocked()
2495		f.resolveRespLock.Unlock()
2496	
2497		f.fileMu.Lock()
2498		if f.file != nil {
2499			f.file.Close()
2500			f.file = nil
2501		}
2502		f.fileMu.Unlock()
2503	
2504		f.setState(statePaused)
2505		return nil
2506	}

2520	func (f *Fetcher) Stats() *fetcher.Stats {
2521		f.connMu.Lock()
2522		defer f.connMu.Unlock()
2523	
2524		terminal := f.getState() == stateDone
2525		prefetched := int64(0)
2526		connectionCount := len(f.connections)
2527		if connectionCount == 0 {
2528			prefetched = f.resolveDataPos.Load()
2529			if terminal && f.meta != nil && f.meta.Res != nil && f.meta.Res.Size > prefetched {
2530				// A small range response can finish entirely during resolve prefetch,
2531				// before a formal connection is created. The fetcher owns this fact, so
2532				// expose one aggregate connection here instead of making Downloader
2533				// infer protocol state from task-level progress.
2534				prefetched = f.meta.Res.Size
2535			}
2536			if prefetched > 0 {
2537				connectionCount = 1
2538			}
2539		}
2540		connectionTotal := f.averageConnectionTotal(connectionCount)
2541		statsConnections := make([]*fhttp.StatsConnection, 0)
2542		for _, connection := range f.connections {
